questions.q: Who carried the luggage and Alan's great-coat as they left the Cage?
choices: One of the gillies from the Cage
Alan himself, on his own strong back
David, though he was still weak
A pony borrowed from Cluny's men
questions.evidence: whither we were led by one of the gillies from the Cage

questions.q: At the start of the march, how did David and Alan each feel?
choices: David was angry and proud; Alan was angry and ashamed
David was cheerful and rested; Alan was sad and tired
Both were happy and glad to be free of Cluny and his cards
David was frightened of the soldiers; Alan was calm

questions.q: Why did David feel ashamed when he thought about separating from Alan?
choices: Leaving the friend in greater danger would be disloyal
He knew he could never find the way home without Alan
He had promised Cluny that he would stay by Alan's side
He owed Alan money and could not pay it back yet

questions.q: What did David think made Alan's conduct over the money "scarce better than theft"?
choices: Alan had wheedled the money from him while he lay half-conscious
Alan had taken the money out of his pocket while he was fast asleep
Alan had given the money to Cluny's gillies without asking him
Alan had lied and said the money was his own from the start
questions.evidence: Wheedling my money from me while I lay half-conscious

questions.q: What did Alan do first when he finally broke the silence beside Loch Errocht?
choices: Said he was sorry
Offered to repay the money
Asked to carry the pack
Began whistling a song
questions.evidence: I have to say that I'm sorry

questions.q: Alan said he had long owed David something, and now owed him money as well. What was it?
choices: His life
His sword
A new coat
An apology
questions.evidence: I have long been owing ye my life

questions.q: Why was Alan unhappy with the route Cluny's scout chose?
choices: It led through the country of the Glenorchy Campbells, his blood-foes
It took them far out of their way, up to the north and the cold sea
It went straight past the camp where the dragoons were waiting
It meant crossing Loch Rannoch in daylight in an open boat

questions.q: Alan calls the Campbell country "one of the dowiest countries in Scotland," with nothing but "heath, and crows, and Campbells." What does "dowiest" mean?
choices: Most dreary and gloomy
Most rich and fertile
Most crowded with people
Most beautiful and green
questions.evidence: There's naething there that I ken, but heath, and crows, and Campbells

questions.q: What was the weather like for most of the three nights they travelled in the mountains?
choices: Misty, windy and almost always raining
Hot and dry, with a blazing sun
Frosty, with deep snow on the high hills
Calm and clear, with a bright moon
questions.evidence: almost continually blown and rained upon

questions.q: What did Alan do when the cry of the river rose unusually sharp?
choices: He crossed himself in the manner of the Catholics
He drew his sword and stood guard at the ford
He told David the old story of the Water Kelpie
He made them lie still until the noise had died away
questions.evidence: to see him cross himself in the manner of the Catholics

questions.q: How did David treat Alan during the first two days of these wanderings?
choices: He refused his help and looked past him like a bush or stone
He talked to him kindly and thanked him warmly for every kindness
He shouted at him every hour and threatened to leave him
He kept asking him to tell stories to pass the time
questions.evidence: passing him over with my eyes as if he had been a bush or a stone

questions.q: What changed in Alan after David coldly refused, perhaps for the ninth time, to let him carry the pack?
choices: He stopped being patient and began to taunt David, calling him Whig
He gave up on David and went off alone to look for a house for the night
He grew even kinder and carried David's pack without asking
He fell silent and would not speak another word for days
questions.evidence: "Whig" was the best name he had to give me

questions.q: Why did David, sick and miserable, begin to like the thought of dying on the mountain?
choices: He imagined Alan would be tortured with regret
He believed he would finally be free of his uncle
He hoped someone would find him and take him home
He thought the soldiers would stop chasing Alan
questions.evidence: Alan would repent then, I thought

questions.q: Why did Alan's whistling of "Johnnie Cope" anger David so much?
choices: It mocked a royal defeat, though Alan himself had fought on the royal side that day
It was the song the dragoons had played when they camped upon the moor
It reminded David of the stormy night his uncle sent him up the tower in the dark
It was a Campbell song, and Alan only sang it to make fun of Colin Campbell
questions.evidence: Alan, on the day of that battle, had been engaged upon the royal side

questions.q: What did David do after his insults, when Alan said some things cannot be passed over?
choices: Drew his sword and fell on guard
Turned his back and walked away fast
Fell to the ground in a swoon
Begged Alan to forgive him
questions.evidence: drawing my sword, I fell on guard

questions.q: What did Alan do instead of fighting David?
choices: Threw his sword away and fell to the ground, saying he could not
Knocked David's sword from his hand with one quick stroke
Laughed at David and then walked off whistling a tune into the night
Called for Cluny's scout to come and carry David away
questions.evidence: he had thrown it from him and fallen to the ground

questions.q: Since no apology could undo his words, how did David bring Alan back to his side?
choices: He put away his pride and simply cried for help
He offered to give Alan all the money from Cluny
He told Alan the Campbells were not his friends
He promised never to call Alan a Stewart again
questions.evidence: a mere cry for help might bring Alan back to my side

questions.q: Why is it funny when Alan agrees David may be "a foot, or near hand" taller?
choices: Alan, proud of his size, eats his words so as not to start a new quarrel
Alan was in fact much taller than David and had only been teasing him all along
David had made up the whole thing to see if Alan was listening
Alan had always said that height did not matter to a real soldier
questions.evidence: to hear Alan eat his words up in the fear of some fresh quarrel

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: A bitter quarrel that nearly ends the friendship, healed when David is sick
The two friends fighting a long duel with swords in which Alan is badly wounded
David and Alan agreeing to separate and take different roads
A long, easy journey through friendly Stewart country
questions.evidence: and now I like ye better!
